title: Reading the result: significance, minimum detectable effect and decision

videos.script: Three weeks, fifty thousand visitors, and a result. The new checkout converted four point six seven per cent, the old one four point two eight. {{rates}} Is that a win? The p-value says the difference is unlikely to be chance: zero point zero three. By the plan written in lesson 7, that means ship. {{plan}} But the p-value is the least informative number on the page. {{least}} The interval says the true lift is somewhere between almost nothing and three quarters of a point. The plan's minimum worth shipping, six tenths of a point, is inside it. So is zero point zero three. {{interval}} And lesson 9 showed that most of the lift came in the first week. {{novelty}} Reading a result is putting those three things side by side, and deciding. This lesson reads Panela's result the way it should be read, and then makes the decision, with the reasons written next to it. {{end}}
